title: Establish lateral consensus and escalation matrix for PRD review & tight-scope decisions
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: PRD reviews for medium-scope runtime and telemetry changes are frequently stuck in async threads, causing delayed launches and ad-hoc scope splits. Objective: Create a lightweight lateral-consensus process and an explicit escalation matrix so PRDs can be reviewed and accepted within a compact window (3 business days for non-blocking items, 7 business days for items requiring legal/security). Deliverables: 1) Consensus playbook (decision thresholds, required approvers by track), 2) Escalation matrix with time-boxed steps and contacts, 3) A short RACI note included in PRDs, 4) Template sign-off checklist and example filled PRD for runtime telemetry change. Constraints: Must not add heavy ceremony; keep self-serve for low-risk items and escalate only when dependencies or data residency/security implications exist.
acceptance_criteria: Consensus playbook published in Confluence with clear decision thresholds and approver lists
Escalation matrix documented with primary/secondary contacts and SLAs for each escalation step
PRD sign-off checklist template created and used for the next two PRDs in scope
At least one cross-team tabletop exercise completed with Engineering, Design, Legal, and Security
Measured review latency reduced: median time to final sign-off for medium-scope PRDs reduced from >10 days to <=7 days over next two cycles

A: Product (Mateo Chen) - own execution and stakeholder nudges

notes: Tabletop exercise agenda: 1) Walk a runtime telemetry PRD through the playbook, 2) Enact escalation when legal flags data residency, 3) Time-boxed decisions and rollback criteria
Example thresholds: low-risk=changes to UI text or non-sensitive metrics; medium-risk=runtime perf, batching, cache behavior; high-risk=telemetry export, customer data flows, third-party vendors

Escalation path: 1) Triage owner (48h) -> 2) Product manager + track leads (72h) -> 3) Tri-party panel (Eng/Legal/Security) (additional 48h) -> 4) Exec escalation (if unresolved after 7 business days)
